section: Mughal painting, music, language and literature; Persian-Sanskrit translation movement
subsections: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign

accepted.s:
Who among the following Persian masters was brought to India by Humayun and helped lay the foundation of the Mughal school of painting?
1. Mir Sayyid Ali
2. Abdus Samad
3. Ustad Mansur
4. Basawan
accepted.x: Mir Sayyid Ali and Abdus Samad were the two Persian masters brought by Humayun. Ustad Mansur and Basawan belonged to the later Mughal painting tradition.
accepted.tq: Identify the two associated names before eliminating painters from later reigns.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Mughal school of painting gradually developed from Persian miniature painting into which type of style?
o: A geometric style based exclusively on Central Asian art
A symbolic style without human figures
A purely religious and monochromatic style
accepted.x: The style gradually moved from Persian miniature painting towards a realistic and colourful Indian style.
accepted.tq: Choose the precise description of the artistic transition rather than an extreme or exclusive alternative.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Emperor)
a. Humayun
b. Akbar
c. Jahangir
d. Shah Jahan

List-II (Emphasis)
i. Formal court scenes, albums and floral borders
ii. Foundation through Persian masters
iii. Illustrated manuscripts and a large painting atelier
iv. Portraits, albums, flora, fauna and naturalism

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Humayun is associated with the Persian masters; Akbar with illustrated manuscripts; Jahangir with naturalism; and Shah Jahan with formal court scenes and floral decoration.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and match the distinctive artistic emphasis of each emperor.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Akbar's painting atelier:
1. It was known as the Tasvir Khana.
2. It had more than 100 painters.
3. It produced illustrated versions of the Hamzanama, Tutinama, Akbarnama and Razmnama.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Akbar's Tasvir Khana was a large atelier of more than 100 painters and worked on the listed illustrated manuscripts.
accepted.tq: Check whether all the components of the atelier description belong to the same reign.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Hamzanama, depicting the tales of Amir Hamza, was a major illustrated project of the atelier of which Mughal emperor?
accepted.x: The Hamzanama was a huge illustrated project undertaken in Akbar's atelier.
accepted.tq: Use the emperor–project association to distinguish Akbar's manuscript programme from later court painting.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following features is most characteristic of Jahangir's painting tradition?
o: Portraits, albums, flora and fauna, and refined naturalism
Exclusive use of floral borders with heavy gold decoration
Large-scale manuscript illustration as the principal emphasis
Withdrawal of imperial patronage and dispersal of painters
accepted.x: Jahangir's period represented the zenith of Mughal painting, especially in portraiture, albums, flora, fauna and naturalistic representation.
accepted.tq: Match the most distinctive cluster of features with Jahangir's reign.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The introduction of the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head in Mughal painting is associated with the reign of:
accepted.x: Jahangir's painters introduced the halo or nimbus behind the emperor's head, reflecting the period's refined and naturalistic style.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive visual innovation against neighbouring emperors.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Shah Jahan's painting tradition, consider the following statements:
1. Formal court scenes were prominent.
2. Albums called muraqqas received attention.
3. Floral borders and extensive use of gold were characteristic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three features are associated with Shah Jahan's formal and richly decorative painting tradition.
accepted.tq: Verify each element of a reign-wise art profile before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The withdrawal of imperial patronage to painters during the reign of Aurangzeb contributed to the growth of painting centres in which of the following regions?
1. Rajasthan
2. Punjab Hills
3. Bihar
4. Bengal
accepted.x: Painters moved to Rajasthan, the Punjab Hills and Bihar after Aurangzeb withdrew patronage. Bengal is not included in this association.
accepted.tq: Find the one geographically added region that does not belong to the stated dispersal pattern.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basawan — Jahangir's specialist in flora and fauna
Ustad Mansur — Akbar's leading manuscript illustrator
accepted.x: Abdus Samad was a Persian master associated with Humayun and Akbar and was given the title Shirin Qalam. Ustad Mansur was associated with Jahangir and Basawan with Akbar.
accepted.tq: Use the title–painter association while rejecting swapped reigns and specialities.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Ustad Mansur is particularly associated with which aspect of Mughal painting?
accepted.x: Ustad Mansur, a painter of Jahangir's court, was renowned for depicting flora and fauna.
accepted.tq: Separate a painter's artistic speciality from literary and architectural activities.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Manohar was the son of Basawan.
2. Manohar was associated with portrait painting in the Akbar–Jahangir period.
3. Basawan was one of the leading masters of Akbar's court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Manohar, the son of Basawan, worked in the Akbar–Jahangir period and was known for portraits, while Basawan was a leading Akbar-era master.
accepted.tq: Link family relationship, artistic speciality and reign without confusing the two painters.
accepted.sec: Painting - Persian masters, Hamzanama, emperor-wise emphasis, painters → reign  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Akbarnama is correct?
o: It was written by Khafi Khan during Aurangzeb's reign.
It consists of three volumes, the third being the Ain-i-Akbari.
It is a critical account of Akbar's religious policy by Badauni.
It was written by Jahangir as his autobiography.
accepted.x: The Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl in three volumes, with the third volume known as the Ain-i-Akbari.
accepted.tq: Use the volume relationship to distinguish closely related Mughal works and authors.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ain-i-Akbari is best described as:
o: A biography of Aurangzeb's first ten years
A detailed administrative report of Akbar's empire
accepted.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, the third volume of the Akbarnama, provides a detailed account of Akbar's administration and empire.
accepted.tq: Identify the work by its function rather than by the emperor associated with its subject.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgir)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)
a. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
b. Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh
c. Padshahnama
d. Alamgirnama

List-II (Author)
i. Abdul Hamid Lahori
ii. Mirza Muhammad Kazim
iii. Nizamuddin Ahmad
iv. Abdul Qadir Badauni

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad; Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh by Badauni; Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori; and Alamgirnama by Mirza Muhammad Kazim.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure chronicle–author pair and eliminate codes with swapped Mughal writers.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following authors wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, a work critical of Akbar's religious policy?
accepted.x: Abdul Qadir Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh, which was critical of Akbar's religious policy.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work association while distinguishing Badauni from Abul Fazl.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The attribution of Tabaqat-i-Akbari to which of the following writers is correct?
accepted.x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Abdul Qadir Badauni wrote the Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused Mughal historical works and their authors.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Abdul Hamid Lahori wrote the Padshahnama. Alamgirnama was written by Mirza Muhammad Kazim, Futuhat-i-Alamgiri by Ishwardas Nagar, and Muntakhab-ul-Lubab by Khafi Khan.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched pair among several author substitutions.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Alamgirnama, dealing with the first ten years of Aurangzeb's reign, was written by:
accepted.x: Mirza Muhammad Kazim wrote the Alamgirnama, which covers the first ten years of Aurangzeb's reign.
accepted.tq: Use the chronological coverage of the work to identify its author among neighbouring chroniclers.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who wrote Futuhat-i-Alamgiri?
accepted.x: Futuhat-i-Alamgiri was written by Ishwardas Nagar and deals with Aurangzeb's reign.
accepted.tq: Test the exact author of a less frequently recalled Mughal chronicle.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Mughal literary works:
1. The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is an autobiography.
2. Jahangir patronised the dictionary Farhang-i-Jahangiri.
3. The Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Jahangir wrote the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri, patronised Farhang-i-Jahangiri, and Khafi Khan wrote the Muntakhab-ul-Lubab.
accepted.tq: Combine related literary facts while checking that each author and work belongs to the correct period.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Tuzuk-i-Baburi from the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
o: The former is Akbar's administrative report, whereas the latter is Badauni's chronicle.
The former is Babur's memoir, whereas the latter is Jahangir's autobiography.
Both are administrative reports written by Abul Fazl.
Both are Persian translations of the Mahabharata.
accepted.x: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, or Baburnama, is Babur's memoir, while the Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is Jahangir's autobiography.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar titles by identifying their respective imperial authors and genres.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Abul Fazl's Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, mentions Diwali and compares it with which festival?
accepted.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated 1590, mentions Diwali and compares it with Shab-e-baraat.
accepted.tq: Link the date and the specific comparative cultural reference instead of choosing a generally associated festival.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The term 'Rekhta', in the context of the rise of Urdu, refers to a linguistic development involving the combination of:
accepted.x: Rekhta developed through the combination of Persian, Hindi and regional dialects, contributing to the rise of Urdu.
accepted.tq: Identify the constituent languages of a composite linguistic tradition without adding unrelated classical languages.
accepted.sec: Book → author (Akbarnama to Futuhat-i-Alamgiri)  [APPSC]
